title: Juniper and the Summit
premise: Yara Iversen, a storm chaser deep in debt to the Meridian Trust—a lending collective whose cheerful enforcers never stop smiling—takes a salvage contract to recover equipment left behind by a vanished government survey team in the Kestrel Range. Following the river upstream, she discovers the team didn't die: they found the source, a geothermal vault that records and replays sound from decades past, including a transmission proving the Trust's founder falsified the surveys her own father died mapping. Hunted by both the Trust's collectors and a survey survivor who wants the truth buried, Yara must choose between selling the recording to clear her debt and broadcasting it, knowing loyalty to her father's memory may cost her everything. In the end she releases the data publicly, walks away owing nothing but grief, and finally belongs—to herself.
about_author: Lior Almeida is the pen name of a former field hydrologist who spent six seasons mapping remote watersheds before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels where landscapes are characters and every debt—financial or emotional—comes due.

chapters.title: The Smiling Men
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A debt collector with unnerving warmth gives her one week before the Trust seizes her storm-chasing rig. Desperate, she accepts a salvage contract: retrieve the vanished survey team's gear from the Kestrel headwaters. Emotional beat: cornered pride hardening into resolve as she signs a contract she doesn't fully read.

chapters.title: Gear With No Tracks
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the abandoned basecamp she finds intact tents, full food stores, and boots lined up neatly—as if the team walked out barefoot into a blizzard. No bodies, no tracks, only a river gauge still ticking. Emotional beat: unease curdling into obsession; the wilderness feels like it's watching her back.

chapters.title: Upstream Rules
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, intercut with diary fragments of survey leader Dr. Ansel Voss. She follows the river canyon through rockfall and rising water, learning the terrain forgives nothing. The diary hints the team found 'something that listens.' Emotional beat: grudging respect for the missing team becoming companionship with the dead.

chapters.title: The Other Survivor
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She catches a figure shadowing her: Petra Lindqvist, the survey team's comms officer, alive and hostile, claiming she alone escaped. Petra warns Yara to turn back—and reveals the Trust funded the original survey. Emotional beat: distrust; two survivors circling each other, each certain the other is the trap.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Flashback: the team reached the source, a geothermal cavern whose stone conduits replay sounds absorbed decades ago—including voices. Petra heard her dead brother's voice there and fled rather than face it. Emotional beat: grief exposed; her hostility toward Yara revealed as fear of returning.

chapters.title: The Collectors Arrive
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The Trust's enforcers reach the range by helicopter—not for salvage, but to seal the source permanently. Their leader, ever-smiling Dane Okafor, offers to erase Yara's debt if she guides them in and says nothing about what they find. Emotional beat: temptation; the price of silence looks exactly like freedom.

chapters.title: Voices in the Vault
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Evading the collectors, Yara and an unwilling Petra enter the cavern. Among the replayed voices Yara hears her father's final radio call—and hears what really happened on his last survey: the Trust falsified his maps, and he died exposing it. Emotional beat: shattering recognition; memory becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Debt Too
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra confesses she was paid by the Trust to bury the team's findings and let the disappearance stand; the others chose to stay at the source rather than lie. She begs Yara to take the buyout—for both their sakes. Emotional beat: betrayal and pity entwined; Petra's confession is also a plea.

chapters.title: The Source Seals
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Climax. Okafor's crew detonates the access canyon while Yara broadcasts the vault's recordings on the survey team's emergency band, forcing every listening station in the region to log the truth. Petra turns on the collectors to buy Yara time; the cavern collapses behind them. Emotional beat: sacrifice—truth purchased with the place that held it.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Weeks later, the recordings have gone public, the Trust is under investigation, and Yara's debt is voided by scandal rather than payment. She visits her father's grave, tells him what she heard, and drives toward the next storm—not running, chasing. Emotional beat: quiet belonging; she owes nothing and finally owns herself.
